source_references.excerpt: **CV05 — full request binding.** `allocation_policy` constructs canonical AllocationPolicy: exact integer K≥2 (no hidden upper cap), canonical required_support=(label,positive-int-minimum) tuples with no duplicates, positive integer node_budget (default100000), profile SYNTHETIC_GROUPED_V1, search_limit18, objective LEX_EVENT_LABEL_ORIGINAL_SQUARED_IMBALANCE_V1, role_policy CANONICAL_EVENT_DEVELOPMENT_ONLY_NO_FALLBACK_V1, allow_ungrouped_fallback=False exactly, schema SYNTHETIC_ALLOCATION_POLICY_V1. bool/float integers reject. Same profile string with different K/support/budget is a different request. Do not reuse receipts under changed policy or reconstruct expected policy from a candidate. Every fallback request other than exact False rejects. Source: `src/railway_detection/synthetic/grouped_cv.py:397-429` (`AllocationPolicy`); `src/railway_detection/synthetic/grouped_cv.py:432-436` (`allocation_policy`).

**CV06 — deterministic feasibility.** Validated development groups are ordered by descending original count then canonical ID. Greedy evaluates K choices using sufficient statistics and lexicographic squared imbalance (event count, per-label count, original count), tie-breaking by fold. It verifies nonempty folds and required per-fold label support. This objective guides the heuristic; it does not promise the global optimum. Greedy failure at≤18 events invokes deterministic bounded first-feasible DFS with fold symmetry reduction/support pruning; larger failure is undetermined. No random seed or ungrouped fallback substitutes for constraints.

To avoid this, freeze model generation prospectively or use a nested selection scheme whose model for e has no e-dependent selection. Calibrator fitting may use the valid OOF scores/labels as explicitly allowed calibration exposure; that does not make those same cases independent final evaluation. source_references.excerpt: **CB05 — distinct metrics.** Let di=(ti−t(i−1))/1,000,000, qi be the end angle, and b(q)=1 iff q≤45 exactly. Event endpoint duration is `Σ di*b(qi)` over emitted sensor/timer/cutoff intervals. The continuous estimator integrates b(q(t)) under the declared clipped linear dynamics. LOWER from q>45 contributes max(0,d−(q−45)/vdown), otherwise d; RAISE from q≤45 contributes min(d,max(0,(45−q)/vup)), otherwise 0; HOLD contributes d*b(q). Clip angles to [0,90]. A single equality instant has zero continuous measure; HOLD at45 contributes all its duration. No epsilon broadens θ≤45°.

Three factual corrections are confirmed: (1) parameter count is 25,697, not "approximately 25,000"; (2) the 10 Hz cadence originates from `decision_policy_v1.yaml` while the frozen experiment config uses 0.2 s (5 Hz), creating a documented but unresolved dual-rate configuration; (3) F1/AUC metrics are report-only with no independent real-crossing validation. Two limitations are documented: the operating threshold lacks independent validation on real crossing acoustics, and ESC-50 negative training data may not represent field conditions. No contradiction was found between the original audit's architectural claims and the source code. The audio subsystem correctly enforces RULE_2 (support-only) and the V2 prohibition in executable code.

source.excerpt: **CB01 — synthetic command boundary.** `CausalRunner` accepts already-decided commands. It has no controller callback, media loader, file writer or incremental public actuator API. Required future integration must own a separately selected coordinator and retain frame-to-decision-to-command correspondence. A command fixture proves actuator behavior only. Keep the private reporting helper internal; arbitrary overlapping/gapped interval records are outside its preconditions.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: **CB02 — exact clock ownership.** Legacy float conversion is explicit: finite nonnegative float → shortest-round-trip decimal → exact-grid validator. 0.2 is accepted; `0.1+0.2` and `3*0.2` reject. Required adapter retains original lexical/tick/float representation and chosen conversion profile alongside normalized µs. Clock accuracy, synchronization and camera relationships are caller/researcher evidence, not established by exact arithmetic. No silent rounding or cross-camera synchronization is permitted.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: **CB03 — issue versus application.** At accepted origin t0 the configured angle is unchanged; issue u0 at t0 with effective time t0. For each next accepted boundary ti, integrate the previously active command over [t(i−1),ti], record its origin/effective time and resulting angle, then issue ui. Zero configured command latency means ui affects only future positive intervals. No pre-origin integration. A requested CLOSED command never means instant physical closure. A terminal command may be logged without contributing duration.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: **CB04 — mode and failure contract.** ARRIVAL consumes in supplied order. A structurally valid ID/time with t≤last accepted sensor time produces DUPLICATE or OUT_OF_ORDER rejection and does not advance clocks, replace the command, rearm timers or enter accepted IDs. This ordering check precedes target validation, so even an invalid target on an otherwise recognized older/duplicate event is discarded as a rejection. Invalid time or identity is INCOMPLETE. Reused accepted ID at a new later instant is INCOMPLETE. OFFLINE prevalidates every input's type/time/ID/command before actuation, then stable-sorts by (time,input index); duplicate times retain input-order priority. Future invalid inputs can therefore invalidate an OFFLINE run even past cutoff. `reordered` records actual index order changes.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: **CB05 — distinct metrics.** Let di=(ti−t(i−1))/1,000,000, qi be the end angle, and b(q)=1 iff q≤45 exactly. Event endpoint duration is `Σ di*b(qi)` over emitted sensor/timer/cutoff intervals. The continuous estimator integrates b(q(t)) under the declared clipped linear dynamics. LOWER from q>45 contributes max(0,d−(q−45)/vdown), otherwise d; RAISE from q≤45 contributes min(d,max(0,(45−q)/vup)), otherwise 0; HOLD contributes d*b(q). Clip angles to [0,90]. A single equality instant has zero continuous measure; HOLD at45 contributes all its duration. No epsilon broadens θ≤45°.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: **CB06 — effective configuration.** Every status stores the same RunConfiguration snapshot consumed by the run: exact initial/closing/opening values; normalized watchdog; mode; cutoff_us; report_times_us; profile `SYNTHETIC_CONVENTION_B_V1`; schema `SYNTHETIC_RUN_CONFIGURATION_V1`; timestamp_policy `INTEGER_US_OR_EXACT_GRID_DECIMAL_SECONDS_V1`; dynamics `CLIPPED_LINEAR_0_90_STRICT_BLOCKED_LE_45_V1`; command_latency_us=0; watchdog_priority `SENSOR_FIRST_ONE_SHOT_V1`. Unsupported identifiers/latency reject. Constructor defaults must be explicitly recorded as effective defaults. A later runner reconfiguration cannot alter the local active snapshot. Frozen objects do not protect against hostile same-process mutation. Source: `src/railway_detection/synthetic/convention_b.py:124-180` (`RunConfiguration`).

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: **CB07 — non-adopted watchdog profiles.** NONE has no timeout or response. SCHEDULED and DETECT_ON_ARRIVAL require positive exact integer timeout_us and normalized response. SCHEDULED triggers once per accepted-sensor generation at last_sensor+timeout, splitting the trajectory; a valid sensor at equality wins and rearms, while cutoff at equality permits the timer. Rejected sensors do not rearm. DETECT_ON_ARRIVAL acts only on a later accepted sensor with strictly greater gap than timeout; prior motion retains old command, requested intent stays logged, selected response replaces only future command. No later sensor means no detect action, even at extended cutoff. No timer evaluates a controller or proves safety. Researcher adoption is **pending**; future policy-preservation experiments should explicitly select NONE unless separately authorized.

source.excerpt: **CB09 — acceptance of results.** `verify_run_configuration` checks typed expected/current settings, config digest, profile/mode/initial angle/report binding. It does **not** recompute trajectory, validate every result field, authenticate execution or bind event inputs/source code. `canonical_json` uses the result's own settings and is weaker than independent expected-settings acceptance. Required future adapter must retain ordered input + selected configuration + producing code identity + fixture/run identity independently, obtain output from the controlled producer, and compare full deterministic output/recomputed trajectory or independent numerical oracle before accepting detached results. A forged angle/duration with unchanged config can pass config-only verification. A coherently replaced expectation and candidate can also agree. These limitations are acceptable only for trusted synthetic fixtures with that external ownership; no detached result is an authority. Source: `src/railway_detection/synthetic/convention_b.py:246-274` (`verify_run_configuration`).

source.excerpt: **CB10 — complexity.** N input events, S emitted intervals, R report intervals. Fixed merge: O(S+R) arithmetic work and O(1) auxiliary objects; no report slice or sort. Default total reuse adds no lookups. Whole producer: O(N+S+R) stored/temporary objects, including indexed inputs, accepted/rejected/issue logs, intervals, grids, normalized fixed input and canonical configuration copies/JSON. OFFLINE adds O(N log N) sorting and O(N) sort storage; ARRIVAL does not sort. Exact rational operation cost and memory grow with operand bit lengths. The helper is not a bounded-memory whole-run streamer. Finite measurements and no-slice regression support the implementation; callers must bound workload deliberately.

A derivative DAG must be acyclic, parents present, and every parent-child edge resolve to the same canonical event. Multi-parent derivation is allowed only within that event. Descendants preserve event role by membership in that group. Annotation IDs cannot be shared by multiple assets; orphan/missing/wrong joins reject. Group weight counts originals, not inflated derivative count.

Same supplied content_identity across different canonical events rejects as unresolved; never silently merge events. Same content identity inside one event may be represented, and separate original asset records still count separately: no deduplication or near-duplicate discovery is implemented. The caller must settle actual identity upstream. No image/perceptual hashing is authorized. Canonical aliases resolve before allocation and outputs use canonical event IDs only.

One group stays in one fold regardless of captures, cameras, originals, derivatives or annotations. Same camera/crossing may occur in multiple events/folds: this is event grouping, not leave-camera-out validation or proof of independence.

Same profile string with different K/support/budget is a different request. Do not reuse receipts under changed policy or reconstruct expected policy from a candidate. Greedy evaluates K choices using sufficient statistics and lexicographic squared imbalance (event count, per-label count, original count), tie-breaking by fold. It verifies nonempty folds and required per-fold label support. This objective guides the heuristic; it does not promise the global optimum. Greedy failure at≤18 events invokes deterministic bounded first-feasible DFS with fold symmetry reduction/support pruning; larger failure is undetermined. No random seed or ungrouped fallback substitutes for constraints.

Retained RoleContext contains original dataset, allocation, policy, outer_fold, validation_events, calibration_mode, frozen_rule_id. `validate_fit_membership` rebuilds the expected plan, compares it, checks all sibling disjointness/coverage and then proposals. BASE_MODEL_FIT/PREPROCESSOR_FIT/FEATURE_CACHE permit only training; FINAL_REFIT permits training+tuning only with frozen_rule_id; CALIBRATOR_FIT permits only reserved calibration under that mode. Canonical SHA256 binds caller-declared content and detects mismatches against separately retained content; it supplies no keyed verification, signature, trusted storage, scientific truth, human authority or resource permission. Frozen dataclasses are cooperative. Replacing both source/expectation and candidate can pass; deliberate same-process mutation is not sandboxed. Input truth, actual source/transform execution, fit/selection/initialization/exposure evidence and producer identity are outside present verification. source.excerpt: AB13. Adjudication is a separate immutable record binding exact sealed/corrected source digests, appointed adjudicator/conflict decision, applicable evidence and rationale. Unresolved remains UNCERTAIN. Automatic averaging/forced agreement/overwriting is forbidden; independently observed values may coincide with arithmetic midpoints. Active8.1 and proposed8.2 do not become interoperable by fabricating APPROVED or proposal hashes. Any schema extension for new censored/not-observable adjudication outcomes requires R01 and a tested versioned adapter before actual use.

source.section: ## 2. Irreversible human knowledge and observation phases
source.excerpt: AB14. Mandatory six risk categories remain the pending source policy: explicit review flag, UNCERTAIN, engine T3/T4 interpretation, front/back conflict, hash inconsistency/missing evidence, corrected/unverifiable candidate. Censored alone is not a trigger. Unknown trigger input blocks a declaration of fully evaluated review. Required second review and separate adjudication retain both source histories; human agreement cannot cure wrong media identity.

source.excerpt: AB15. PromotionBatch is closed and content-addressed: batch_id, project/protocol/schema/adapter bindings, sorted cohort-qualified output identities, exact source ledger heads and observation/correction/adjudication digests, trigger/appointment/conflict evidence, deterministic output digests and policy digest. ApprovalRecord.subject_digest binds this batch digest, not a free-form event count. Authority reserves a unique batch/content ID; same ID/different bytes conflicts. Publish staged immutable qualified objects create-only, then one protected atomic visible batch manifest/receipt. Readers trust only manifest members; an uncommitted staging prefix is never GT. Crash/revocation semantics follow RC01–RC09. The present promoter is not claimed to implement these obligations.

source.excerpt: RC01. Use canonical UTF-8 JSON: sorted ASCII object keys, no whitespace/BOM, no JSON floats, minimal integers with booleans distinct, exact decimal strings/rational pairs, preserved Unicode scalar text without normalization, quote/backslash escapes, U+0000…001F as lowercase six-character escapes, other scalars literal UTF-8. Reject duplicate/unknown keys, invalid Unicode and noncanonical bytes. Set arrays have type-specific sorted unique keys; order-bearing arrays preserve order. Cross-language golden vectors must cover every representation. Generic JSON defaults do not by themselves implement this codec.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: RC02. RecordBody has exactly schema_version, session_id, record_id, operation_id, sequence, kind, actor_principal, role_binding, approval_binding, grant_binding, assignment_binding or null, phase_binding or null, protocol_binding, execution_binding, previous_record_digest and content. kind is GENESIS, OBSERVATION, CORRECTION, EXPOSURE, ADJUDICATION, RECOVERY, FINALIZE or ABORT. Content is a separately closed type by kind; human kinds require AB11–AB13 fields, exposure requires both source-seal digests and monotone knowledge version, terminal content references only the prior committed head; the resulting terminal digest/head is stored outside its own body in the authority receipt, avoiding self-reference. Genesis sequence=0 and previous_record_digest=null (no zero-hash sentinel); every later sequence=prior+1 and previous_record_digest is the exact prior envelope digest. Genesis content binds grant/session/project/policy and initial fence. Body excludes all computed digests and attestations.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: RC03. body_sha256=SHA256(canonical body). A detached actor attestation binds that digest and approved mechanism/issuer. Envelope has exactly body, body_sha256, actor_attestation; record_digest=SHA256(canonical envelope). Wrapper has exactly envelope, record_digest, followed by one un-hashed newline for framing. Anchor contains session_id, sequence, record_count, byte_length, final_record_digest, authority_version and current_fence. Record count includes genesis. Authenticate expected anchors independently; a locally self-consistent chain cannot prove identity, truth or absence of rollback.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: RC04. Authority serializes reservation, prepare, revocation, lease/fence change, commit and finalize for each affected session/grant using linearizable transactions. Operation states are PREPARED, COMMITTED, ABORTED and UNKNOWN_EXTERNAL. No operation may have two content digests. query(operation_id, authenticated principal) returns exact state, bound digest and immutable receipt or absence; querying never re-executes a side effect. A lease takeover increments the monotone fence; stale owners may damage writable local files but cannot obtain broker use or authoritative commit. Stable-inode local locking is cooperative serialization only.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: RC05. Commit order is: (1) current actor/approval/binding/phase/quota check and PREPARED reservation; (2) durable protected payload journal containing exact candidate bytes/content digest; (3) local create-only append under the same stable-inode read-head/validate/append lock and fsync, plus directory fsync on creation; (4) authority commit CAS rechecks grant/time/revocation/fence/session ACTIVE/expected head and atomically advances anchor, quota/knowledge state and COMMITTED receipt; (5) ACK. Steps2/3 may each leave recoverable uncommitted data; neither alone is success. ACK is forbidden until both protected payload and local append are durable and authority commit is durable. An alternate protected storage architecture must prove equivalent recoverable payload durability before acceptance, not silently omit it.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: RC06. Revocation linearizes by incrementing current revocation version before returning success. Commit after that point must abort PREPARED work if it relies on the revoked authority, even if local append already occurred. A commit that linearized first remains historical COMMITTED; revocation blocks future actions and handle reuse but cannot revoke disclosed bytes. Finalize atomically requires ACTIVE and no outstanding PREPARED/UNKNOWN_EXTERNAL operations; it may return BUSY and must be retried only as authorized. Finalize commit writes the terminal receipt/head and blocks all later prepares/commits. Abort marks remaining PREPARED operations ABORTED, preserves/quarantines their bytes and never unreserves the grant. No arbitrary in-flight IO cancellation is promised.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: RC07. Crash recovery authenticates the same principal/session/project/bindings, a still-valid grant/roles, a fresh exclusive fence and trusted current anchor. COMMITTED but ACK-lost returns the same receipt and never appends again. PREPARED with exact protected bytes may finish only via an explicitly authorized recovery transaction with fresh checks; revoked/expired or changed-content candidates abort/quarantine. A local suffix without matching PREPARED journal cannot be adopted. Missing local COMMITTED bytes are restored from protected journal only via audited recovery that preserves the authoritative bytes/head; missing protected payload is an incident, not a reset from local state. Torn suffix/mid-file corruption is preserved and quarantined. Never truncate acknowledged history silently.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: RC08. External effects use a separate content-bound idempotent transaction. No local ledger can provide global exactly-once IO. Missing external outcome becomes UNKNOWN_EXTERNAL; it blocks finalization/publication until an independently verified receipt resolves it, otherwise quarantine. Promotion visibility uses the single protected batch-manifest commit point from AB15, with revocation/fence/approval recheck. Staging objects alone remain non-authoritative. Replay with exact committed batch returns receipt; different bytes under the same ID conflict.

source_qualified_crosswalk.disposition: Acceptance requirement only; preserve executed-versus-planned distinction

source.excerpt: RC09. Pure security requirements remain blueprint-only. Future synthetic cases must cover every crash cut between RC05 steps, simultaneous prepare/revoke/commit/finalize orderings, stale owners, ACK loss, journal/local loss, torn suffix, quota/knowledge atomicity and authority compromise. The system denies unknown authority state and reports availability loss; it makes no administrator-compromise or physical-railway guarantee.

source.section: ## 2. Closed typed lineage registry and reference graph
source.excerpt: CVL01. The general candidate corpus registry contains versioned immutable tables and no implicit path loading. Binding={artifact_id,version,digest,provenance_role,evidence_status,authority_ref}; status is VERIFIED, NOT_VERIFIED or NOT_VERIFIABLE. Accepted scientific evidence requires actual trusted resolution, not a flag. The deterministic input-reference DAG contains only preexisting input evidence; allocation payload then references inputs; output validation receipt references payload; authenticated execution/approval receipt references payload and validation. No output receipt is required as its own hashed input. A resolver rejects unavailable/conflicting versions, unsupported provenance roles, cycles or mismatched digests. This contract does not cause protected evidence to be accessed.

PhysicalEvent has canonical_event_id, dataset/version/cohort, exact aliases, immutable curator/provenance binding, prospective dataset_role, weather/lighting/direction MetadataValue, declared labels with policy/provenance and exposure records. MetadataValue is {value:string or null, unknown_reason:string or null, provenance_ref}; exactly one value/unknown_reason is populated. Unknowns remain unknown. Alias table is a function to one canonical pass; conflicting aliases reject. Physical-event counts count canonical passes once, not aliases or engine versions. No railway train_events category is detector-training permission.

A recording may contain multiple events; capture identity alone does not merge unrelated passes. Asset has asset_id, canonical_event_id, capture_id or null, kind ORIGINAL_FRAME/STILL/DERIVATIVE/ANNOTATION, parent_asset_ids, frame_index/PTS/timebase or explicit unavailable reason, annotation_ids, transform record or null, content_identity_ref or null, eligibility/exclusion and provenance. Annotation has annotation_id, asset_id, version, labels/explicit confirmed-empty disposition, vocabulary/policy and provenance. Every eligible asset, label and exclusion must join completely. Derivative DAGs must be acyclic and resolve every parent. All ancestors of an accepted derivative must belong to its single canonical physical event and role; excluded parents propagate exclusion. This version rejects every multi-event composite, even if an external policy claims to permit it. Supporting plural origins requires a separately versioned schema/policy/review; no hidden extra key or guessed primary origin is permitted. Established cross-event duplicate-content identity conflicts reject until a separately approved merge/exclusion policy resolves them; known near-duplicate uncertainty blocks independent claims.

source.excerpt: CVL09. For declared K≥2 and each required label's minimum m≥1, require at least K nonempty eligible physical components and at least K*m distinct supporting eligible events per every-evaluation-fold label. These are necessary conditions only. Feasibility output distinguishes INVALID_INPUT, INFEASIBLE_NECESSARY, FEASIBLE_GREEDY, FEASIBLE_SEARCH, INFEASIBLE_EXHAUSTIVE and UNDETERMINED_BUDGET or UNDETERMINED_SIZE. No invalid/undetermined/infeasible result contains an accepted assignment. All labels/support/roles/K are frozen inputs; no automatic K/stratum/role reduction or ungrouped fallback occurs.

source.excerpt: CVL10. Sort components by decreasing original asset count then canonical event ID. Greedily place each in the fold minimizing the tuple (resulting sum of squared event-count imbalance, supplied-label imbalance, original-frame imbalance, fold index), computed from complete aligned records using integers. If the resulting nonempty partition satisfies every required support constraint, return FEASIBLE_GREEDY and recomputed objective/coverage; it is deterministic, not globally optimal. Cost is O(M*K*(L+1)) plus lineage validation/sorting; implementation must not enumerate K^M on this path. Synthetic metadata with thousands of events may test operation and grouping without generating a research split.

source.excerpt: CVL11. If greedy constraints fail and M≤18, search a deterministic depth-first assignment tree in the same component/fold order, bounded by an explicit positive integer node budget. Count root and each visited prefix. Prune empty-fold impossibility and label-support capacity using remaining supporting events. Folds are interchangeable because constraints are identical for every fold; first-use fold-label symmetry reduction may skip equivalent labels. Return first verified feasible leaf as FEASIBLE_SEARCH, never OPTIMAL. Exhausting all canonical branches without a valid leaf proves only these frozen constraints INFEASIBLE_EXHAUSTIVE. Reaching budget returns UNDETERMINED_BUDGET; M>18 after greedy failure returns UNDETERMINED_SIZE. No time-based acceptance, random seed or implicit alternate policy is used. A small independent brute-force synthetic oracle must check feasible/infeasible classifications.

source.excerpt: CVL12. Construct per-iteration role views only from the verified assignment and its exact complement. CALIBRATION_ONLY and reserved/final/case-study groups stay outside allocator/fit/independent evaluation as defined in SC12–SC15. A final refit uses only the outer complement under an explicit frozen rule. Failed inner support/empty subsets block that candidate, not prove every nested plan impossible. 17D does not search globally across nested outer/inner plans or train anything.

source.excerpt: SC02. Timestamp input is an integer number of microseconds (bool rejected), or a finite nonnegative decimal-seconds string exactly on the microsecond grid. pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ### Decision 1 — Minimum review-session duration and handling of suspiciously short sessions
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: **Phase 11.6 recommendation (not a decision — presented for explicit researcher approval, not yet confirmed):** **(D)**, the secondary non-blocking "fast but passing" band. Rationale: (A) risks accepting a genuinely too-fast session outright; (C) is a one-size-fits-all floor that is already acknowledged as not evaluated against real timing data, same weakness as (A) just set higher; (B) requires a formula this document is not positioned to justify without the timing data Decision 1's own "unresolved concerns" note says doesn't exist yet. (D) is the only option that does not require trusting an unvalidated number outright — it converts "was this review fast enough" into "does a second reviewer agree," which is verifiable, at the cost of extra reviewer effort on borderline-fast sessions. **Practical implication:** requires choosing the upper threshold of the "fast but passing" band, which is not specified here and remains open even if (D) is approved. **Trade-off not resolved by this recommendation:** (D) does not, by itself, pick a lower hard floor — some flat minimum (per A or C) would likely still be needed beneath the band, meaning a full implementation needs a combined choice, not (D) alone.

This re-characterizes the finding from "no train present on this camera at all" to "the claimed T3 timestamp is mistimed by roughly 5–10 seconds relative to this camera's actual content" — a pattern consistent with a front/back camera clock or offset-attribution error, not an absent locomotive-clearance event. `event_021` is one of the 16/27 events without a validated R04 front/back offset, so **no corrected numeric T3 value is proposed** — substituting a number here (e.g. "T3 ≈ 8–11s") would itself be an unverified estimate, which this phase's governing instructions explicitly prohibit inferring. Ledger row: `INV_event_021_T3`, classification `UNRESOLVED_REQUIRES_FURTHER_HUMAN_ADJUDICATION`. **Explicitly not extended to `event_021`'s separate T4 (t=60.1s) or `T_scene_clear` ambiguous rows** (`AMB_event_021_T4`, `AMB_event_021_T_scene_clear`) — those concern a different, unexamined part of the recording and remain unresolved with no new evidence this phase.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ### 1.7 — Notice content: proposed vs. completed/authorized (Task 1, item 7)
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: **Minor clarity gap, Finding F4.** The written notice's `disposition` field is a flat `"INVALIDATED"` string, while its provenance fields are named `proposed_by`/`proposed_at_utc`. Once this notice genuinely exists on disk (i.e., real execution has occurred), its existence *is* the applied disposition mechanism — so `"INVALIDATED"` is an accurate statement of what this file represents at that point. But the field naming (`proposed_*`) could read to a future, uninformed reader as "this is still just a proposal," when in fact a written notice is the actual, now-applied marker. The `note` field does clarify non-destructiveness ("does not modify, move, or delete the file it describes") but does not clarify the proposed-vs-applied distinction. Not a safety defect — a documentation/wording clarity issue in a durable artifact.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ## 2. Audit of Previous Mission (`2026-10-30` / `R1`) Claims vs. Actual Code
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: | **A2. B7e Delayed Timestamps (`STALE_TIMESTAMPS`)** | Claimed `FailureMode.STALE_TIMESTAMPS` was hardened to fail closed and isolate `target_source`. | **Three Gaps Found**: (1) `failure_injector.py:170-181` used substring matching (`target_source in r.source_id`) instead of exact equality (`r.source_id == target_source`), allowing `target_source="camera"` to mutate both cameras and unknown sources to silently no-op; (2) repeated invocation compounded delays (`t - 2 * delay_s`) and did not record `original_timestamp_s`; (3) `ExperimentRunner._get_failure_schedules` still returned an unparameterized `STALE_TIMESTAMPS` schedule and `run_condition` checked `failure_schedules` only after simulation. | **Remediated & Verified**: `FailureInjector.inject_failures` validates all `STALE_TIMESTAMPS` schedules upfront, rejects unknown or substring `target_source`, matches exact `r.source_id == target_source`, records `original_timestamp_s` in `r.metadata`, and computes `orig_ts - delay_s` idempotently. `ExperimentRunner` fails closed immediately when `B7e` lacks explicit `failure_schedules`. |
pending_term_discovery_ledger.disposition: discovery hit; may be historical, negation, duplicate, proposal or genuinely open. Canonical item status controls; this hit alone grants/settles nothing.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ## 2. Audit of Previous Mission (`2026-10-30` / `R1`) Claims vs. Actual Code
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: | **A3 & C. Ground-Truth State Safety & Cohort Isolation** | Claimed `premature_opening_window=None` prevented profile assumptions and that cohorts were separated. | **Critical Defect Found**: In `ExperimentRunner.run_condition` (`src/railway_detection/experiments/runner.py:114-144`), `has_train_ground_truth=bool(event.labels)` converted events with **missing** ground truth (`event.labels == ()`) into `has_train_ground_truth=False`, causing `EventMetricsCalculator.evaluate_run` to evaluate missing ground truth as a **confirmed no-train negative control** (`false_alarm_evaluation` / `no_false_alarm`)! Furthermore, non-observable label statuses (`censored`, `uncertain`, `unobservable`) were not filtered out when `timestamp_s` was present, and `clock_aware.evaluate_event_replay` labeled `engine_events` as `"no_false_alarm"` / `"false_alarm_evaluation"` instead of `"engine_event_excluded"`. | **Remediated & Verified**: `EventMetricsCalculator.evaluate_run`, `EventMetricsCalculator.aggregate_cohort`, `clock_aware.evaluate_event_replay`, and `ExperimentRunner._extract_event_ground_truth` now distinguish confirmed train, confirmed no-train, engine, missing, unknown, censored, unobservable, uncertain, and not-applicable states. Missing/unknown ground truth is marked `evaluable=False, notes="ground_truth_missing"` and excluded from both train and negative-control denominators. `engine_events/event_001` is isolated across all paths. |

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ## 1. Can a same-camera (onset, T4) pair be observed? — answered from documents
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: **Why a back-camera "frame-entry" time is not an acceptable substitute for E.** A frame-entry event depends on where the camera is mounted and its field of view; it is a property of the *camera*, not of the *crossing*. The researcher's definition requires an *independently established physical* blocked onset. Using frame-entry would silently redefine the metric to a different physical instant (and a different one at each site). It must not be used unless the researcher defines it as a new, explicitly camera-relative boundary.
pending_term_discovery_ledger.disposition: discovery hit; may be historical, negation, duplicate, proposal or genuinely open. Canonical item status controls; this hit alone grants/settles nothing.

These bound the *candidate* inventory only. The **actual evaluable count today is 0** (no approved GT, R04 unresolved). T0's censoring prevalence does **not** predict T2's; T2's prevalence is unknown.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.text:
| **DEC-C01** (`F-04` / `D-1`) | **Unresolved Decision 1:** What replay start-coverage rule must `classify_m4` enforce before classifying an event without a pre-$T_4$ block as `NEVER_PROTECTED_M5` (or `EVALUABLE` no-violation)? | Currently `classify_m4` checks only `last_step >= T4`. A replay starting after $T_4$ (`[6.0, 7.0]` with $T_4=5.0$) or starting late (`[4.0, 6.0]` unblocked) is classified `NEVER_PROTECTED_M5` from zero or partial pre-$T_4$ observation! | Open HIGH finding `F-04`. Pre-5A test `test_phase12_metric_arithmetic.py:321` pins `[(5, True), (6, True)]` at $T_4=5.0$ as M5. | **Option C01-A (Strict Zero-Start Coverage):** Require `first_step_s == 0.0` (after 1-$\mu$s rounding) and `first_step_s < T4`, else `NOT_EVALUABLE` (`replay_started_late` / `replay_started_at_or_after_T4`) unless a violation is witnessed in `(t_blocked, T4)`.
**Option C01-B (Two-Tier Exact Start Coverage — Recommended):** Always require `first_step_s < T4` (else `NOT_EVALUABLE: replay_started_at_or_after_T4`, updating the pre-5A `[5.0, 6.0]` test). In addition, add parameter `require_start_at_zero: bool = True` (or `expected_start_s: float \| None = 0.0`) so any replay with `first_step_s > 0.0` and no witnessed violation is `NOT_EVALUABLE: replay_started_late` when `expected_start_s=0.0` (which matches `RealEventReplayProducer`'s `0.0` start grid).
**Option C01-C (Minimum 1-Step Pre-T4 Only):** Only require `first_step_s < T4` (so `[4.9, 6.0]` unblocked is still M5).
**Option C01-D:** Keep current behavior and disclose M5 as unchecked for start coverage. | **C01-B** eliminates both failure modes (zero pre-$T_4$ observation and partial late-start `[4.0, 6.0]` observation) **without inventing an arbitrary numeric tolerance cliff** because `RealEventReplayProducer` generates frames deterministically starting at `0.0s` (`collector.py:221`). C01-C leaves a discontinuity between `first_step=4.9` (M5) and `5.0` (`NOT_EVALUABLE`). | Updates `classify_m4` (~12 lines) and updates `test_phase12_metric_arithmetic.py:321` (`late` fixture gets a `(0, False, "OPEN")` step at `t=0` so it tests "never blocked before T4, first blocked at T4" on a full `[0, 6]` replay!). | Prevents false inflation of `NEVER_PROTECTED_M5` from truncated/late-starting replays. M4 denominator unchanged; M5 denominator restricted to replays that actually observed `[0, T4]`. | None. | **Recommend Option C01-B** (see full analysis in §7.1). | **Cat C** | **No** | **Yes (Gate 1)** | No | Blocks Phase 1 WP 1.1 & M4/M5 contract closure. |

| **DEC-C02** (`F-05` / `D-2` / `BR-20`) | **Unresolved Decision 2:** How should `classify_m4` treat a replay that reaches $T_4$ (`last_step >= T4`) and has $t_{\text{blocked}} < T_4$, but has **zero retained steps strictly inside** $(t_{\text{blocked}}, T_4)$? | In Mission 5A, `no_steps_in_protection_interval -> NOT_EVALUABLE` was implemented conservatively, but this conflates two distinct physical situations: (1) a sparse/unsampled replay (`[0.0, 5.0]` with `max_step_gap_s = 5.0`), vs (2) a dense normal replay (`tick = 0.2s`) where the barrier first blocked on the **last tick before $T_4$** (e.g., steps at `4.6` open, `4.8` blocked, `5.0` blocked, with $T_4 = 5.0$). | Open MEDIUM finding `F-05` / `BR-20`. Currently returns `NOT_EVALUABLE` (`no_steps_in_protection_interval`) for both. | **Option C02-A (Keep Conservative Single Rule — Recommended Default):** Keep `no_steps_in_protection_interval -> NOT_EVALUABLE` for all empty `(t_blocked, T4)` intervals and report `max_step_gap_s` diagnostically.
**Option C02-B (Split Reason Codes, Both `NOT_EVALUABLE` — Recommended Enhancement):** Keep status `NOT_EVALUABLE` (no numeric tolerance!), but split the reason into `no_steps_in_protection_interval` (when `t_blocked` and `T4` are separated by no interior step) and record `first_blocked_s`, `last_step_s`, and `max_step_gap_s` so downstream tables distinguish late blocking near $T_4$ from sparse sampling.
**Option C02-C (Revert to Vacuously Safe):** Return `EVALUABLE, premature=False`. | **C02-A / C02-B** uphold the core safety principle ("never count zero interior observation as safe `premature=False`") and avoid inventing a step-gap threshold. C02-C is scientifically unsafe because a 2-step replay `[0.0, 30.0]` would be declared "protected through T4". | Under C02-A/B, production classification logic stays `NOT_EVALUABLE` with zero tolerance; C02-B adds diagnostic clarity in summary reporting. | Excludes zero-interior-step events from M4 and M5 denominators with an explicit reason instead of claiming continuous protection. | None. | **Recommend Option C02-A (with C02-B diagnostic fields)** (see §7.2). | **Cat C** | **No** | **Yes (Gate 1)** | No | Blocks Phase 1 WP 1.1 & GD-2 approval. |

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: #### 1. Exact Failure Scenario in Current Production Code
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: - **Failure Mode X2 (Zero Pre-$T_4$ Observation):** Suppose $T_4 = 5.0\text{ s}$, and the replay contains retained steps only at $t \in \{5.0, 6.0\}$ (or $t \in \{6.0, 7.0\}$). The replay observed **zero ticks strictly before $T_4$** (`[0, 5.0)` was completely unobserved). Yet because `last = 6.0 >= 5.0` and no step has `t_blocked < 5.0`, `classify_m4` returns `M4_STATUS_NEVER_PROTECTED` (`never_protected = True`), asserting an empirical safety failure (M5: "barrier never blocked before $T_4$") from **zero pre-$T_4$ evidence**.

The interval $[0.0, 4.0)$ was never observed (for instance, due to a partial stream or dropped head frames), during which the barrier might or might not have been blocked. Again, `classify_m4` classifies the event as `NEVER_PROTECTED_M5` (`never_protected = True`).

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: #### 5. Key Insight on Why M4 vs M5 Start Coverage Differs
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: - **For M4 (`t_blocked < T4`):** The M4 interval is `(t_blocked, T4)`. Since `t_blocked` is the timestamp of a retained step in `sim_result.steps`, `first_step_s <= t_blocked` holds automatically! Therefore, as soon as `t_blocked < T4` and `last_step_s >= T4` (with $\ge 1$ interior step), the entire interval `(t_blocked, T4)` is bracketed on both ends by retained steps. (The only subtlety is if the replay started at `t = 2.0` already blocked, so an earlier block at `t = 1.0` followed by a reopening at `t = 1.5` was missed; requiring `first_step_s == 0.0` for `replay_complete=True` catches that too unless a violation is already witnessed in `(t_blocked, T4)`.)
pending_term_discovery_ledger.disposition: discovery hit; may be historical, negation, duplicate, proposal or genuinely open. Canonical item status controls; this hit alone grants/settles nothing.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: #### 5. Key Insight on Why M4 vs M5 Start Coverage Differs
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: - **For M5 (no blocked step before $T_4$):** M5 asserts that the barrier *never* blocked during $[0, T_4)$. To assert a universal negative over $[0, T_4)$, the replay **must have started at `0.0` (`first_step_s == 0.0`) and reached `T4` (`last_step_s >= T4`)**. If `first_step_s >= T4`, it observed nothing before $T_4$ (`replay_started_at_or_after_T4`). If `0.0 < first_step_s < T4`, it missed $[0, \text{first\_step\_s})$ (`replay_started_late`).

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ### C4.2. PROPOSED exact search / tie-breaking / stopping
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: This PROPOSED objective prioritizes physical-event balance, then the preselected feature distribution, then frame-count balance; the final assignment vector breaks all ties deterministically. pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ### C4.2. PROPOSED exact search / tie-breaking / stopping
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: PROPOSED reference procedure: traverse the full prefix tree in depth-first order; extend the next sorted component with fold indices0,1,…,K−1 in that order. Count every visited prefix, including the root, as one node. No unstated randomized branch ordering, symmetry pruning or heuristic early acceptance is permitted. At each complete leaf, evaluate the hard constraints applicable to that run level from the frozen role policy; invalid leaves are discarded. OUTER runs map assigned fold to OUTER_EVAL and its complement to OUTER_TRAIN_POOL; INNER runs map assigned fold to INNER_TUNE and its complement to INNER_TRAIN. Only the corresponding Support rules are applied at that level; outer-evaluation exclusions always apply to inner inputs. EVERY_FOLD_COVERAGE targets OUTER_EVAL for an outer run and INNER_TUNE for an inner run. Compute the exact integer objective at each valid leaf and retain its lexicographic minimum. If all nodes are exhausted with no valid leaf, report INFEASIBLE_EXHAUSTIVE. If all are exhausted with a minimum, report FEASIBLE_OPTIMAL. If the next node would exceed node_budget, report UNDETERMINED_BUDGET and publish **no accepted assignment**, even if an incumbent exists; an optional diagnostic incumbent is explicitly non-accepted and never written as a split manifest. A time limit is not substituted for the deterministic node budget.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ### C4.3. PROPOSED outer/inner allocation and verification
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: Freeze the chosen outer assignment without model feedback. For each outer fold i, OUTER_EVAL is exactly groups assigned i; OUTER_TRAIN_POOL is its DEVELOPMENT_POOL complement. If tuning_mode=INNER_GROUPED, repeat the same deterministic reference procedure with the declared inner K/configuration using only that complement, recomputing its counts and support feasibility. Inner assignments reference the immutable outer-assignment digest. If tuning_mode=FROZEN_RULE, no inner split is generated and the prospectively frozen training/threshold/early-stopping rule digest is mandatory. Neither mode may inspect outer outcomes. No automatic choice between them exists. Outer FEASIBLE_OPTIMAL establishes only that outer run, not inner feasibility. Every required inner run must independently complete successfully before an accepted nested payload exists; an inner failure/budget limit blocks publication of the whole candidate. It does not prove that every alternative outer partition/nested plan is infeasible. There is no automatic reshuffle, role change or K reduction; the unresolved design returns to T03/R03/R06.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ## H7. PROPOSED ledger serialization, commit, recovery and audit
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: PROPOSED canonical record encoding: UTF-8 JSON, no BOM/whitespace/final newline in the hashed body; lexicographically sorted ASCII field names; integers/booleans/null/strings/arrays/objects only, no JSON floating numbers or NaN/infinity. Object field names and identity keys are printable ASCII. Human text values may contain any Unicode scalar value; reject unpaired surrogates. Preserve text exactly with no normalization. JSON strings escape quote and backslash with their two-character escapes; U+0000…U+001F use lowercase six-character \u00xx escapes, never short escapes; slash and all other Unicode scalars are emitted directly as UTF-8. Integers use minimal base10 with no plus/leading zeros/negative zero; booleans/null use the standard lowercase JSON literals. Exact decimal seconds use nonnegative decimal strings with no exponent, leading zeros or trailing fractional zeros (zero is 0); raw_entry_text retains the original human lexical entry/precision. Rational PTS/timebase values use integer numerator/positive-denominator pairs reduced to lowest terms where a rational value is encoded. No numeric normalization changes an already SEALED record. Arrays retain their declared order; set-valued arrays use the explicitly prescribed exact-key sort. Unknown/duplicate keys, invalid encoding and noncanonical bytes are rejected. A future encoder/version and cross-language golden vectors need T01/T04 acceptance; this is not a claim about current schema serialization.
pending_term_discovery_ledger.disposition: discovery hit; may be historical, negation, duplicate, proposal or genuinely open. Canonical item status controls; this hit alone grants/settles nothing.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ## H7. PROPOSED ledger serialization, commit, recovery and audit
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: PROPOSED digest rule: record_body includes schema/session/record_id/sequence/kind/human principal, role-policy/authentication-session references, exact content/provenance and previous_record_digest. It excludes the actor attestation and both computed digests. Compute body_sha256 over those canonical body bytes. A detached actor_attestation binds body_sha256 through the selected trusted mechanism. Form the canonical envelope with exactly body, body_sha256 and actor_attestation; record_digest is SHA-256 of that complete envelope. Append the canonical wrapper with exactly envelope and record_digest plus one newline. The next record links this envelope-derived record_digest. This two-level construction avoids a signature/self-hash cycle while binding the complete attestation into the chain and protected anchor. The genesis binds session/grant/policy/protocol identity; every later record links its actual predecessor. A trusted committed anchor binds session_id, last sequence, record count, byte length, final digest and monotonic authority version; trusted genesis alone cannot detect suffix truncation. Actor attestations bind the body, not merely an untrusted handle. A digest's integrity meaning never becomes an authenticated signature by naming it “signature.”

pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: **CB07 — non-adopted watchdog profiles.** NONE has no timeout or response. SCHEDULED and DETECT_ON_ARRIVAL require positive exact integer timeout_us and normalized response. SCHEDULED triggers once per accepted-sensor generation at last_sensor+timeout, splitting the trajectory; a valid sensor at equality wins and rearms, while cutoff at equality permits the timer. DETECT_ON_ARRIVAL acts only on a later accepted sensor with strictly greater gap than timeout; prior motion retains old command, requested intent stays logged, selected response replaces only future command. No later sensor means no detect action, even at extended cutoff. No timer evaluates a controller or proves safety. Researcher adoption is **pending**; future policy-preservation experiments should explicitly select NONE unless separately authorized.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ### 2.2 Physical Boundary Distinctions and Hazard Interval
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: - **Premature opening** is defined by the selected M4/M5 profile in the companion protocol (`first_blocked_to_t4_clearance`, v9.1.1-PROPOSED §5.2), not by a $T_1$-based window. It requires an approved observable $T_4$ and a replay timeline; ground truth supplies only $T_4$, never $t_{\text{blocked}}$. Replay-evidence rules (zero-origin coverage for M5, strict open interval, `no_steps_in_protection_interval` as not evaluable, no sampling-density threshold) are defined in v9.1.1-PROPOSED §5.2.1 and are not restated here. Ground-truth boundary values and replay timestamps are compared on the one-microsecond grid `round(float(t), 6)` with strict comparisons; this is a floating-point representation fix, not a timing tolerance, and the review tolerance remains DEFERRED (RD-012).

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ### 5.2 Physical Hazard Interval and Metric Formulas
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: - **Premature Opening (M4) — selected profile `first_blocked_to_t4_clearance` (RD-014; Phase 1 contract).** For a train event with an approved, observable $T_4$ on the replay's own timeline, let $t_{\text{blocked}}$ be the timestamp of the first retained replay step whose passage is blocked (the *observed* first blocked state), provided $t_{\text{blocked}} < T_4$. The event is a **premature opening** iff some retained step strictly inside the open interval $(t_{\text{blocked}}, T_4)$ has the passage unblocked or a gate state of `OPENING`/`OPEN`. M4 is a per-event yes/no result, **not a duration**. The interval is open at both ends and **no timing tolerance** is applied. Ground truth supplies only $T_4$; $t_{\text{blocked}}$ always comes from the replay.
pending_term_discovery_ledger.disposition: discovery hit; may be historical, negation, duplicate, proposal or genuinely open. Canonical item status controls; this hit alone grants/settles nothing.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: 2. **Witnessed violation.** A violating step retained strictly inside $(t_{\text{blocked}}, T_4)$ is definite and M4-evaluable (`premature = true`) even if the replay ends before $T_4$ or began after the recording origin.
pending_term_discovery_ledger.disposition: discovery hit; may be historical, negation, duplicate, proposal or genuinely open. Canonical item status controls; this hit alone grants/settles nothing.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: 4. **Sufficient observation of the protection interval.** M4 requires at least one retained step strictly inside $(t_{\text{blocked}}, T_4)$. If none exists, the event is `NOT_EVALUABLE` with reason `no_steps_in_protection_interval` (DEC-C02): it is not safe, and not a premature opening. Diagnostics are retained (`first_step_s`, `first_blocked_s`, `last_step_s`, `interior_step_count`, `max_step_gap_s`). No nominal tick size and no step gap is used to infer protection; **no maximum-gap or sampling-density threshold exists or is introduced**.
pending_term_discovery_ledger.disposition: discovery hit; may be historical, negation, duplicate, proposal or genuinely open. Canonical item status controls; this hit alone grants/settles nothing.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: 5. **M4 needs no zero-origin replay.** Its interval begins at the observed first blocked step, so an event is not excluded merely because the replay began after $t = 0$. (A replay that begins already blocked cannot reveal a close-and-reopen that preceded its first retained step; M4 does not claim to.)
pending_term_discovery_ledger.disposition: discovery hit; may be historical, negation, duplicate, proposal or genuinely open. Canonical item status controls; this hit alone grants/settles nothing.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: 6. **Never Protected (M5) — counts only (RD-017).** A replay is classified M5 only if (a) its first retained step is at the zero origin ($t = 0$ on the grid), (b) it reaches $T_4$ (`last retained step ≥ T4`), and (c) no retained step before $T_4$ is blocked. A first blocked step exactly at $T_4$ is *not before* $T_4$ and is still M5 if (a) and (b) hold. A replay whose first step is **at or after $T_4$** is `NOT_EVALUABLE` (`replay_started_at_or_after_T4`); any other replay whose first step is after the origin is `NOT_EVALUABLE` (`replay_started_late`). Neither is ever M5. No start tolerance is defined: the origin is the exact start of the recording timeline. M5 is reported separately, as counts only, and is excluded from the M4 denominator.
pending_term_discovery_ledger.disposition: discovery hit; may be historical, negation, duplicate, proposal or genuinely open. Canonical item status controls; this hit alone grants/settles nothing.

The two outcomes are kept distinct.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.section: ## 9. Limitations (RD-053; to be stated in the paper)
pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: Single site; a small number of sessions; one cohort of 23 train events, which yields wide intervals; no cross-site, cross-device, weather or night generalization claim; recordings begin after the train is visible in many events (left-censored $T_0$); about 120.8 stream-seconds of no-train exposure is insufficient for a false-alarm rate; a single engine pass; M5 is replay-relative and has no density requirement; sampled replay does not establish continuous barrier state; the physical entry landmark and therefore $T_2$ and full occupancy duration are deferred; the decision policy and its constants were developed after seeing these recordings (pilot contamination) and carry no scientific approval; barrier timing is simulated; ground truth is single-reviewer unless an external audit reviewer is appointed; inter-camera offsets are unresolved; thresholds and ROI are not scientifically approved; historical B0–B7f outputs are diagnostic only; no additional recordings are planned in this study. No certification (SIL, EN 50126/50128/50129) is claimed or implied; the software must not be connected to physical actuators.

pending_term_discovery_ledger.text: Roadside multimodal sensing is investigated as a potential approach to railway-crossing monitoring; cost-effectiveness and deployment suitability are not evaluated here. This paper specifies an auditable descriptive-evaluation framework for a 27-event multimodal recording cohort from a single fixed crossing in Bangladesh (`crossing_A`). It formalizes fail-closed outcome contracts: premature opening (M4) over the strict open protection interval $(t_{\text{blocked}}, T_4)$, never-protected failure (M5) requiring full $[0, T_4)$ temporal observation, and missed-train detection (MTR) conditioned on physical lead-in feasibility screening. It encodes a proposed, not-yet-adopted second-review policy, a model-independence firewall, and isolation of engine movements and negative controls from pooled metrics. Because formal real-data evaluation and human adjudication remain pending researcher authorization, all empirical evaluation figures remain pending placeholders. The contribution is a methodology and engineering specification, not an evaluated real-world system.
